rendered: The review starts from the total known global cobalt reserves, taken from the United States Geological Survey 2021[1] report on cobalt: (7 million metric tons)[2] It then recomputes how much of that is usable for batteries by assuming a conservative yearly mining efficiency of ≈70%[3] and that ≈40% of the mined cobalt directed toward battery manufacturing[4]. The review does not print the intermediate arithmetic, but the stated end result is ≈2 million metric tons[5] globally. Under this reduced figure, the review argues that battery demand would exceed the cobalt available for battery manufacturing before 2045[6], as shown in the model of cobalt depletion in the Figure panel c.
